jobs.title: Director, Digital & Information Management
jobs.description:
Overview

Director, Digital & Information Management is a leadership role responsible for developing and implementing the digital strategy and information management framework for one of our major new build projects. The role is responsible for developing and implementing the digital strategy and information management framework for this project. The Director reports functionally to the Vice-President, Digital Solutions and operationally to the Project Director.

This Director ensures that all project data, documentation, and digital systems are integrated, secure, and aligned with company standards, regulatory requirements, industry standards, and project objectives. The position drives digital transformation to enable efficient collaboration, lifecycle data management, and regulatory compliance across engineering, procurement, construction, and commissioning phases.

Key responsibilities include leading project teams, developing work execution plans, recruiting and assigning team members, managing project deliverables, organizational structure, budget, schedule, risk management, and overseeing people forecasting and levelling for the project.

Your role

Lead the development and execution of the Digital and Information Management strategy for a large-scale nuclear new build project.
Align digital initiatives with project objectives, corporate standards, regulatory requirements, and long-term asset lifecycle management.
Champion digital transformation through BIM, digital twins, data analytics, advanced collaboration platforms, and emerging technologies.
Establish and govern enterprise-wide information management frameworks, including data governance, metadata standards, and document control processes.
Ensure compliance with nuclear industry regulations, cybersecurity standards, and industry best practices such as ISO 19650 and IEC 62645.
Implement and manage integrated digital systems, including BIM, EDMS, project controls, scheduling, cost management, ERP, and asset information platforms.
Lead the deployment of Common Data Environments (CDE) and Advanced Work Packaging (AWP) solutions across EPCM partners, suppliers, and stakeholders.
Oversee project-wide BIM execution, ensuring cross-disciplinary integration, interoperability, data quality, and a single source of truth for project information.
Establish robust cybersecurity, digital safety, training, and corrective action programs to protect critical systems and ensure regulatory compliance.
Monitor digital performance, drive stakeholder adoption, report on system effectiveness and data integrity, and identify opportunities for continuous improvement and cost optimization.

About You

Minimum 10 years of leadership experience in digital transformation, information management, or IT management within large infrastructure, engineering, energy, or industrial projects.
Strong expertise with BIM, Common Data Environments (CDE), Electronic Document Management Systems (EDMS), and project controls platforms.
Experience with integrated 3D engineering design technologies such as Hexagon SmartPlant/Smart 3D, AVEVA, or comparable plant design systems.
Knowledge of nuclear new build projects, reactor design, construction execution, and nuclear industry operating practices is preferred.
Proven ability to lead teams, manage direct reports, and support project delivery organizations through complex digital initiatives.
Solid understanding of Advanced Work Packaging (AWP), engineering, procurement, and construction workflows within large capital projects.
Familiarity with ISO 19650 information management standards, cybersecurity frameworks, and nuclear regulatory compliance requirements.
Strong commitment to nuclear safety culture, industrial safety programs, quality assurance standards, and continuous regulatory compliance.
Demonstrated leadership, stakeholder engagement, communication, customer relationship, and organizational management skills with the ability to drive change.
Proven ability to exercise sound judgment, accountability, teamwork, delegation, problem-solving, and decision-making while performing effectively in high-pressure environments.

Rewards & benefits

Explore the rewards and benefits that help you thrive – at every stage of your life and your career at AtkinsRéalis in Canada.

Enjoy competitive compensation, employee recognition, and a brilliant range of flexible benefits you can tailor to your health, wellbeing, financial and lifestyle needs.

Make the most of diverse opportunities for training and professional development to grow your skills and expertise.

And take advantage of our hybrid working culture and generous time-off policies to balance a fulfilling career with your personal life.

Be rewarded. Find out more.

We're AtkinsRéalis, a world-class engineering services and nuclear organization. We connect people, data and technology to transform the world's'infrastructure and energy systems. Together, with our industry partners and clients, and our global team of consultants, designers, engineers and project managers, we can change the world. We're committed to leading our clients across our various end markets to engineer a better future for our planet and its people.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Technology Risk Assessments
jobs.description:
Requisition ID: 278455

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

Scotiabank is seeking a transformational senior leader to modernize how technology and cybersecurity risks are assessed across the Bank. Reporting to the Vice President, IT Governance & Risk Oversight within the Office of the Chief Information Officer, the Senior Director, Technology Risk Assessments leads Scotiabank's global first-line technology and cybersecurity assessment capability relating to the Bank’s Threat Risk Assessments and Vendor Security Review processes.

The Senior Director brings the Bank's Threat Risk Assessment and Vendor Security Review processes under one leadership responsibility, creating an integrated approach to assessing internally developed technology solutions and third-party technology services. Together, these form an integrated Assessment Authority: one first-line capability for technology and cybersecurity assessment that preserves specialized expertise while introducing common leadership and strategic direction, coordinated intake and triage, consistent assessment methods and risk language, shared evidence and quality principles, reusable platform and security patterns, stronger risk reporting and traceability, modern workflows and structured data, and progressive use of artificial intelligence (AI) and automation.

This role is broader than traditional assessment delivery. It is an enterprise leadership and transformation opportunity to turn fragmented, document-heavy processes into an integrated, risk-based and evidence-informed assessment lifecycle. It brings together technology risk, cybersecurity, security advisory, third-party risk, cloud and AI security, Governance, Risk and Compliance (GRC) modernization, adoption of ServiceNow Integrated Risk Management (IRM), data and automation, and leadership of a global team.

You Will Shape And Lead Six Connected Themes

Integrated Assessment Authority: One accountable leadership model for Threat Risk Assessment (TRA) and Vendor Security Review (VSR), with common direction, methods and risk language across specialized assessment teams.
Shift-left security assessment: Technology and cybersecurity risks identified and addressed earlier in architecture, design and delivery, when they are least costly to resolve.
Platform and application assessment: A two-level model that assesses shared platforms once and focuses application and vendor assessments on what is genuinely specific.
Evidence-informed risk decisions: Risk conclusions grounded in structured, verifiable evidence and consistent rating criteria rather than document volume.
Modern workflow, data and automation: Assessments run through modern ServiceNow IRM workflows, supported by structured data and the progressive use of AI and automation.
Portfolio risk insight: Clear, traceable reporting that surfaces recurring and systemic risks across the Bank's technology and third-party portfolio.

The Platform And Application Model Works At Two Levels

Horizontal assessments evaluate common platforms, shared services and approved technology patterns once, so related controls and evidence can be reused.
Vertical assessments evaluate the application, workload, project, vendor or material change, and focus on specific deviations, exposures and residual risks

Is this role right for you? In this role, you will:

Lead the existing TRA and VSR capabilities under one senior leadership model, preserving specialized expertise while establishing common direction, coordinated intake and triage, and shared standards.
Define and maintain consistent assessment methodology, risk-rating criteria, quality requirements, evidence principles and finding taxonomies, aligned to the Bank's technology control objectives and enterprise control library and to recognized frameworks such as the National Institute of Standards and Technology Cybersecurity Framework (NIST CSF), ISO/IEC 27001 and the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS).
Embed technology and cybersecurity assessment earlier in architecture, design and technology delivery, including the Bank's delivery framework, architecture review processes and Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery (CI/CD) pipelines.
Establish reusable security and platform patterns that allow downstream assessments to inherit approved baselines.
Assess material application-specific and vendor-specific risks, including data, identity, integration, architecture, exposure and residual risk.
Strengthen threat modelling and scenario-based risk analysis, using recognized approaches such as STRIDE and MITRE ATT&CK.
Act as the business owner for the technology-risk assessment capability within ServiceNow IRM, defining assessment requirements, workflows and data needs while working with the technical platform team, which owns platform configuration and delivery.
Lead the assessment-domain transition from legacy processes and repositories into modern IRM workflows, preserving application-to-assessment and application-to-risk traceability and establishing clear data-quality requirements.
Define risk-based triggers for reassessment following material change, significant vulnerability, control failure or deviation from an approved pattern.
Establish targeted post-implementation assurance for selected material controls, using authoritative evidence from accountable control owners and specialist functions.
Prioritize appropriate AI and automation opportunities across intake, triage, context extraction, pattern matching, assessment drafting, evidence orchestration and portfolio insight, in alignment with the Bank's enterprise artificial intelligence and technology-risk automation initiatives.
Identify recurring and systemic risks across the assessment portfolio and provide clear risk insight to technology leaders and governance forums.
Produce assessment outcomes that are timely, consistent, traceable, evidence-informed and defensible for regulatory, second-line, quality assurance and Internal Audit review, including under the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) Guideline B-13 and the New York State Department of Financial Services (NYDFS) Part 500 cybersecurity regulation, where applicable.
Lead and develop a large, multidisciplinary and geographically distributed team, building capabilities in security advisory, cloud and AI security, third-party security risk, methodology, data and automation..

Critical Partnerships

Success depends on strong partnerships across the Bank's three lines of defense. Each partner keeps its established mandate, and the Senior Director works with them to ensure that assessment conclusions are well-informed and aligned. Key partners include:

Technology leadership: Chief Information Officers (CIOs) and their delivery, architecture and engineering teams, the primary clients of the assessment capability.
Cybersecurity and architecture: The Office of the Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) and Enterprise Architecture, to align security standards, patterns and design guidance.
Control owners and control testing: Teams that implement and operate controls, and the Bank's technology control testing function, whose evidence informs assessment conclusions.
Technology risk management: Technology risk teams and Risk and Control Self-Assessment (RCSA) teams, which manage and aggregate technology risk across the Bank.
Platform and automation: The ServiceNow IRM platform and implementation teams, and the Bank's enterprise artificial intelligence and technology-risk automation initiatives, to ensure aligned workflows and data.
Governance and reporting: IT risk governance, issue management and reporting teams within the Office of the Chief Information Officer.
Independent oversight: Second-line risk management, Internal Quality Assurance (IQA) and Internal Audit, which provide independent challenge and assurance, and the teams that manage the Bank's regulatory relationships

Skills

Do you have the skills that will enable you to succeed in this role? We'd love to work with you if you have:

University degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Security or a related field.
10+ years of progressive experience in technology risk, cybersecurity or risk assessment, including senior leadership of technology or cybersecurity risk assessment functions.
Deep expertise in security advisory, assessment methodology and threat modelling at enterprise scale.
Strong experience in third-party and vendor security risk, and in cloud, AI, application and platform security.
A track record of leading enterprise GRC transformation, including with ServiceNow IRM or a comparable GRC platform, from business requirements through adoption.
Strong understanding of development, security and operations (DevSecOps) practices and secure-by-design principles.
Experience engaging regulators and Internal Audit in a highly regulated environment, ideally financial services.
Proven ability to lead large, distributed teams and to lead through influence across federated organizations and with senior technology executives.

Preferred Experience

Advanced degree or professional certifications such as Certified Information Systems Auditor (CISA), Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP), Certified in Risk and Information Systems Control (CRISC) or Certified Information Security Manager (CISM).
Experience leading platform- and pattern-based assessment models that allow controls to be inherited across applications and workloads.
Hands-on experience with risk data, evidence orchestration and workflow automation, including integrations with security tooling.
Familiarity with AI, machine learning and agentic AI applications in GRC, such as intake triage, artifact analysis, control mapping and risk-theme identification.
Experience applying structured risk-rating criteria, calibration and quantitative risk techniques.
Experience partnering with control-testing functions to integrate authoritative control evidence into risk assessment, ideally within a large financial institution

What's in it for you?

Diversity, Equity, Inclusion & Allyship - We strive to create an inclusive culture where every employee is empowered to reach their fullest potential, respected for who they are, and are embraced through bias-free practices and inclusive values across Scotiabank. We embrace diversity and provide opportunities for all employee to learn, grow & participate through our various Employee Resource Groups (ERGs) that span across diverse gender identities, ethnicity, race, age, ability & veterans.
Accessibility and Workplace Accommodations - We value the unique skills and experiences each individual brings to the Bank and are committed to creating and maintaining an inclusive and accessible environment for everyone. Scotiabank continues to locate, remove and prevent barriers so that we can build a diverse and inclusive environment while meeting accessibility requirements.
Upskilling through online courses, cross-functional development opportunities, and tuition assistance.
Competitive Rewards program including bonus, flexible vacation, personal, sick days and benefits will start on day one.
Community Engagement - no matter where you choose to work from; we offer opportunities for community engagement & belonging with our various programs such as hackathons, contests, Humans of Digital and much more.

Location(s): Canada : Ontario : Toronto

Scotiabank is a leading bank in the Americas. Guided by our purpose: "for every future", we help our customers, their families and their communities achieve success through a broad range of advice, products and services, including personal and commercial banking, wealth management and private banking, corporate and investment banking, and capital markets.

jobs.title: Technology Program Management, Vice President
jobs.description:
Do you want your voice heard and your actions to count?

Discover your opportunity with Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG), one of the world’s leading financial groups. Across the globe, we’re 150,000 colleagues, striving to make a difference for every client, organization, and community we serve. We stand for our values, building long-term relationships, serving society, and fostering shared and sustainable growth for a better world.

With a vision to be the world’s most trusted financial group, it’s part of our culture to put people first, listen to new and diverse ideas and collaborate toward greater innovation, speed and agility. This means investing in talent, technologies, and tools that empower you to own your career.

Join MUFG, where being inspired is expected and making a meaningful impact is rewarded.

Summary

The Vice President manages multiple technology projects and teams, establishes governance and stakeholder communications, coordinates dependencies and resources, oversees schedules and reporting, and provides executive updates on strategy, budgets, risks, controls, and delivery. The role also tracks technology expenditures, manages project budgets and capital investments, negotiates internal resources and vendor proposals, and improves project management processes, tools, training, and methodology

Education

Degree or equivalent work experience equally preferable.
Bachelor's degree in computer science or related field.

Certifications

PMP certification preferred.

Work Experience

Technology program management experience in large, cross-organizational projects, prioritizing competing demands, scoping large efforts, and negotiating timelines.

Strong experience within a technology organization in the banking or financial services industries. Regulatory reporting domain exposure is a plus.

Demonstrated ability to manage multiple and diverse projects and initiatives, including analytical thinking, planning, prioritizing, problem solving, decision-making, and carrying out assigned projects and activities with minimal supervision.

Successfully managed large-scale and complex initiatives independently, from start to finish, with a duration of at least six months.

Prior business analyst experience and/or operational expertise preferred.

Experience and knowledge of change management principles, methodologies, and tools preferred.

Familiarity with AI and leveraging AI to improve day-to-day activities and optimization of TPM tasks.
Functional Skills

Business & Strategic Acumen: Understands the business, the industry, and the role IT plays in driving financial success. Aligns technology strategy with organizational goals and vision to deliver stakeholder value.

Enterprise & Architecture Knowledge: Proficient in process and data modeling, architectural development, and IT planning methodologies. Has extensive knowledge of the enterprise's business and decision-making processes.

Technical Breadth: Has deep knowledge across multiple technical environments. Understands software and hardware requirements and implementation steps and translates them into business and program-level terms.

Delivery Methodologies: Proficient in SDLC project and process management tools and methodologies. Has experience with agile, scrum, or hybrid approaches.

End-to-End Project Execution: Has a solid understanding of the full technology project lifecycle. Identifies dependencies and sequences work efficiently.

Release & Risk Management: Demonstrated ability to manage software release risks, including holding releases when necessary.

Vendor Management & Negotiation: Negotiates beneficial terms for software and services agreements in support of project delivery.

Leadership: Builds, leads, and empowers interdisciplinary, geographically dispersed teams.

Continuous Improvement & Planning: Is planning- and process-oriented and introduces new processes or delivery methods as needed.
Foundational Skills

Demonstrates leadership, leads by example, and acts with integrity.

Communicates effectively and serves as a trusted advisor to senior leadership.

Applies analytical and critical thinking, iterative problem-solving, and sound judgment to identify multiple paths to success in a complex environment.

Operates strategically to support continuous improvement and systems thinking, informed by industry trends and best practices.

Builds consensus and collaborates across functions, divisions, and organizations to drive large-scale initiatives and overcome obstacles.

Is flexible, decisive, resilient, and open to others' ideas, and inspires innovation and continuous learning.

Is organized and detail-oriented, with experience reporting to senior management.
Responsibilities
High-Level Responsibilities

Lead teams to support projects on implementation issues. Develop and execute review sessions for high-impact projects. Develop descriptions for project justification, plans, roles, responsibilities, and reporting structure.

Provide training and consulting for project managers and administrators. Provide technical and analytical guidance to project teams. Set the frequency and type of interactions, extent of stakeholder involvement, and develop a dispute resolution process.

Monitor the effectiveness of project management methodology and tools and recommend improvements, as appropriate. Ensure effective communication among business process owners, project team members, and all IT functions that participate in and impact project development results.

Implement enhancements and upgrades to project management processes and tools. Develop proposals, work plans, training plans, budgets, and reports for IT projects.

Detailed Responsibilities

Perform hands-on program management for multiple technology development projects and teams.

Establish project governance, working groups, and stakeholder communications.

Stay abreast of industry trends, actively adopting new practices and techniques to accelerate delivery.

Partners with business, program management, architecture, system owners, third-party vendors, testing, and other teams as necessary to ensure successful delivery.

Drive planning at various organizational levels to ensure projects are on track and appropriately resourced.

Ensure timetables and deliverable schedules are understood and communicated.

Manage dependencies proactively, coordinating across teams to resolve issues and mitigate risks.

Align, plan, and precisely manage activities and dependencies across development teams to ensure cohesive delivery.

Contribute to executive-level updates on strategy, budget, project delivery, controls, risks, and related topics.

Organize and oversee required reporting for business and technology management review sessions.

Track financials related to technology expenditures, including software, hardware, and resource allocation.

Ensure the firm's capital investment is managed efficiently; manage project budgets so maximum allotments are not exceeded.

Manage stakeholders and customers.

Negotiate business and IT resources for project allocation.

Negotiate vendor proposals and manage vendor relationships.

jobs.description:
Job Type:
Permanent Work Model:
Remote Reference code:
135844 Primary Location:
Toronto, ON All Available Locations:
Toronto, ON; Edmonton, AB; Ottawa, ON

Our Purpose

At Deloitte, our Purpose is to make an impact that matters. We exist to inspire and help our people, organizations, communities, and countries to thrive by building a better future. Our work underpins a prosperous society where people can find meaning and opportunity. It builds consumer and business confidence, empowers organizations to find imaginative ways of deploying capital, enables fair, trusted, and functioning social and economic institutions, and allows our friends, families, and communities to enjoy the quality of life that comes with a sustainable future. And as the largest 100% Canadian-owned and operated professional services firm in our country, we are proud to work alongside our clients to make a positive impact for all Canadians.

By living our Purpose, we will make an impact that matters.

Have many careers in one Firm.
Enjoy flexible, proactive, and practical benefits that foster a culture of well-being and connectedness.
Learn from deep subject matter experts through mentoring and on the job coaching

The intended structure of this role is a non-relocation secondment. By nature of this structure, existing employees will remain aligned to their current location, level, service line/business area, salary, and compensation/performance review cycle, for the duration of their secondment to Deloitte Global.

The Director, Global Hosting Services, defines, leads, and governs Deloitte Global’s private-cloud hosting strategy, data center and cloud networking services, and Global Wide Area Network (GWAN). The role oversees secure, resilient connectivity among Deloitte Global hosting facilities, member-firm environments, and cloud service provider (CSP) hubs across Azure, AWS, and Google Cloud. The Director also leads CSP cost reporting and invoice reconciliation through the Deloitte Cloud Services (DCS) Cloud Business Office, supports agile delivery of platform and network enhancements, and ensures operational excellence and rapid incident response across these services.

Key Responsibilities:

Deloitte Cloud Services (DCS) Networking

Oversee the design and implementation of network architecture supporting DCS hubs, connectivity among Deloitte environments, the internet, and cloud service providers, and secure access to cloud-hosted services, including firewalls and load balancers:
Multi-CSP connectivity
Inter-CSP connectivity
Secure hybrid-cloud IPv4/IPv6 connectivity
CSP inter-region global connectivity
CSP intra-region scalability
IP addressing management

Lead the team in delivering these services, with operational excellence and 24/7 monitoring and support.
Drive continuous improvement and automation through API enhancements and agentic AI solutions to reduce service-delivery time and enable proactive monitoring, rapid issue identification, and resolution.

What will your typical day look like?

Interfirm Network Service (GWAN)

Lead the Interfirm Network Service (INS), providing seamless, secure, resilient, and optimized connectivity among member firms and across public-cloud environments.
Develop solution roadmaps and architectures that address evolving business needs, technology requirements, cybersecurity threats, and demand for high-performance, low-latency connectivity.
Drive operational service excellence, support member-firm disaster recovery testing exercises, and adapt connectivity options as firms implement local in-country WAN and SD-WAN solutions.
Manage IPv4/IPv6 address allocation for member firms and countries.

Deloitte Cloud Services (DCS) Cloud Business Office

Provide scaled agile delivery services supporting product enhancements for DCS platform, product, and networking teams, as well as Global Enterprise Cloud Management Services.
Lead Cloud Business Office delivery of CSP cost insights for member firms, CSP invoice reconciliation, and billing to Deloitte entities. Support FinOps through cost-optimization recommendations, CSP cost reporting, and AI token-ledger reporting.

Risk Management & Compliance

Ensure all data center and cloud-platform solutions comply with global regulatory, security, and privacy standards.
Proactively identify risks and implement mitigation strategies.
Serve as a trusted liaison to Cyber teams on cloud-related matters, champion Cyber initiatives, and review and provide feedback on Cyber standards and programs.

Private Cloud Delivery (Colocation Services)

Define and continuously evolve Deloitte Global’s private-hosting and colocation strategy, including regional services in the United States and Germany. Adapt the strategy to emerging requirements such as zero-trust networking, private infrastructure supporting GPU-intensive AI workloads, and future quantum-computing capabilities.
Lead the team in delivering these services while maintaining operational excellence and compliance with audit, SOC, and ISO requirements.
Develop private-cloud roadmaps, standards, and reference architectures, and establish governance frameworks, policies, and cost-recovery processes.

About The Team

Deloitte Technology works at the forefront of technology development and processes to support and protect Deloitte around the world. In this truly global environment, we operate not in what is but rather what can be to help Deloitte deliver and connect with its clients, its communities, and one another in ways not previously conceived.

Enough About Us, Let’s Talk About You

Bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer science, information technology, or a related field.
15 or more years of progressive technology leadership, experience leading infrastructure teams and developing strategy, architecture, or platforms, setting priorities and goals to meet global business goals and objectives
Deep expertise in leading data center and networking teams.
Proven experience in designing, governing, and operating enterprise-scale private-hosting and global networks.
Strong background in automation and operational leadership.
Ability to plan, organize, and manage multiple responsibilities; provide technical direction through project completion; and deliver high-quality outcomes within target timeframes.
Demonstrated ability to drive change and influence senior stakeholders.
Excellent communication, leadership, and organizational skills.
Experience managing global, distributed teams.
Deep understanding of the latest technology, market and trends

Total Rewards

The salary range for this position is $140,000 - $260,000, and individuals may be eligible to participate in our bonus program. Deloitte is fair and competitive when it comes to the salaries of our people. We regularly benchmark across a variety of positions, industries, sectors, targets, and levels. Our approach is grounded on recognizing people's unique strengths and contributions and rewarding the value that they deliver.

Our Total Rewards Package extends well beyond traditional compensation and benefit programs and is designed to recognize employee contributions, encourage personal wellness, and support firm growth. Who We Are

Gildan is a leading manufacturer of everyday basic apparel, with a strong portfolio of brands, including Gildan®, Hanes®, Comfort Colors®, American Apparel®, ALLPRO™, GOLDTOE®, Peds®, Bali®, Playtex®, Maidenform®, Bonds®, as well as Champion® which is under an exclusive licensing agreement for the printwear channel in the U.S. and Canada.

Gildan operates with a strong commitment to industry-leading labour, environmental and governance practices throughout its supply chain in accordance with its comprehensive ESG program embedded in Gildan's long-term business strategy. The opportunity

Reporting to the Principal Accounting Officer, the Director Consolidation & Financial Operations is a strategic leader responsible for the monthly close and consolidation process, as well as the corporate finance & accounting processes for operations, supply chain and cost of sales reporting. The Director Consolidation & Financial Operations is responsible for providing Corporate guidance to the divisional finance teams, coordinating/supporting the external audit process, leading new financial reporting system implementations and upgrades, and managing key vendor relationships.

Lead finance related projects to improve processes, leverage financial systems and support financial operations projects. Coordinate and implement the integration of the financial systems and accounting procedures and controls during acquisitions, and operational and tax reorganizations.
Support the treasury department in movement of funds.

Review of Executive level reporting packages

Provide support for the quarterly and annual external financial statements, MD&A and earnings release (responsible for certain notes and tables).
Aid in the preparation and review of various regulatory filings (MD&A, Press releases, AIF).

The Requirements

University degree in Finance, Accounting, or a related field.
CPA designation required.

jobs.description:
Senior Director, Finance – The Mustard Seed

This executive search is conducted by Nelson/Kraft & Associates on behalf of The Mustard Seed

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

The Mustard Seed is searching for a seasoned and collaborative financial leader with initiative and drive to join their team as Senior Director, Finance.
The Senior Director, Finance is the CFO’s principal operational finance leader and trusted second-in-command. The role provides enterprise leadership across accounting, financial reporting, grants, budgeting and forecasting, treasury, audit, internal controls, finance systems, and process improvement. The successful candidate combines deep Controller-level technical expertise with strong people leadership, sound judgment, and the ability to translate financial complexity into practical decisions that support The Mustard Seed’s mission and long-term sustainability.
If you are an experienced CPA and team leader who comes from a mid to large sized organization with similarly complex moving parts, we would love to hear from you!

WHO WE ARE

The Mustard Seed is a Christian humanitarian organization whose vision is to build community, grow hope, and support change. Intentionally following Jesus Christ and partnering with the community, The Mustard Seed combats the root causes of poverty in Alberta, British Columbia, and Saskatchewan and works to create positive, lasting change in the lives of those we serve. The Mustard Seed provides basic services (food, clothing, housing, and support services), education, and employment to those living in poverty in the locations we serve.

OUR HISTORY

Pat Nixon founded The Mustard Seed in 1984 with a single street ministry location in central Calgary. Today, the organization operates in multiple cities – Calgary, Edmonton, Red Deer, Medicine Hat, and Grande Prairie in Alberta, Kamloops in British Columbia, and Saskatoon in Saskatchewan. All locations offer a different range of programs and services to serve our most vulnerable community members.

Programs & Services Include:

Basic Needs – emergency shelter, meals, clothing and hygiene items
Health and Wellness
Housing
Employment
Spiritual Care
Community Engagement
Community Impact Centres

IDEAL CANDIDATE PROFILE

The ideal candidate is a senior CPA finance leader with deep Controller-level technical expertise and a successful record of leading finance functions in a complex, larger organization. They have personally led significant year-end audits, overseen accounting and financial reporting, managed grant-funded operations, strengthened internal controls, improved budgeting and forecasting, and led finance systems and process transformation. They are equally comfortable resolving a technical accounting issue, guiding a manager, challenging a budget assumption, working with auditors and funders, and advising the CFO and Executive Team. The successful candidate will provide dependable operational leadership while helping modernize Finance and strengthen The Mustard Seed’s financial sustainability, stewardship, and organizational capacity.

QUALIFICATIONS

Education & Professional Designations, Required

Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation in good standing.
Bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance, commerce, business administration, or a related discipline.
Ongoing professional development in accounting standards, financial reporting, governance, internal controls, audit, risk management, and finance leadership.

Preferred Assets

CRMA, CFE, CIA, or another relevant risk, controls, audit, fraud, or governance designation.
Advanced training or certification in ERP systems, data analytics, business intelligence, financial systems implementation, finance transformation, or project management.

Experience Requirements

Approximately 12 to 15+ years of progressive finance and accounting experience, including significant senior leadership responsibility.
A minimum of 5 to 7 years of leading managers and professional finance teams in a large or larger mid-sized, complex organization.
Significant experience serving in a Controller, Corporate Controller, or equivalent senior controllership role, with accountability for the integrity of financial reporting, accounting operations, internal controls, and close processes.
Extensive experience leading the annual external audit from planning through completion, including audit schedules, working papers, issue resolution, management responses, and relationships with external auditors and governance committees.
Demonstrated leadership across financial reporting, general accounting, grants accounting, budgeting and forecasting, treasury, internal controls, risk management, and audit coordination.
Substantial experience with grant-funded operations, including grant budgeting, restricted funding, contribution agreements, eligible expenditures, cost allocations, claims, financial reporting, compliance, funder audits, and closeout.
Experience leading finance systems and process improvement, including ERP optimization or implementation, systems integration, reporting automation, data quality, business intelligence, and finance workflow redesign.
Experience building, restructuring, developing, or stabilizing a finance function while maintaining reliable day-to-day delivery.
Experience advising executives and presenting clear, decision-focused financial information to senior leadership and governance bodies.

Strongly Preferred

Experience in a large charity, not-for-profit, healthcare, public sector, social services, affordable housing, or similarly complex mission-driven environment.
Experience managing a large portfolio of municipal, provincial, federal, or other government funding agreements.
Deep practical experience with fund accounting, restricted contributions, contribution revenue recognition, capital projects, and government-funded initiatives.
Experience with Salesforce-based ERP environments such as Certinia/FinancialForce, budgeting and forecasting tools, Tableau or similar BI platforms, and broader data governance initiatives.

new_jobs.title: Senior Director, Technology Risk Assessments
new_jobs.description:
Requisition ID: 278455

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

Scotiabank is seeking a transformational senior leader to modernize how technology and cybersecurity risks are assessed across the Bank. Reporting to the Vice President, IT Governance & Risk Oversight within the Office of the Chief Information Officer, the Senior Director, Technology Risk Assessments leads Scotiabank's global first-line technology and cybersecurity assessment capability relating to the Bank’s Threat Risk Assessments and Vendor Security Review processes.

The Senior Director brings the Bank's Threat Risk Assessment and Vendor Security Review processes under one leadership responsibility, creating an integrated approach to assessing internally developed technology solutions and third-party technology services. Together, these form an integrated Assessment Authority: one first-line capability for technology and cybersecurity assessment that preserves specialized expertise while introducing common leadership and strategic direction, coordinated intake and triage, consistent assessment methods and risk language, shared evidence and quality principles, reusable platform and security patterns, stronger risk reporting and traceability, modern workflows and structured data, and progressive use of artificial intelligence (AI) and automation.

This role is broader than traditional assessment delivery. It is an enterprise leadership and transformation opportunity to turn fragmented, document-heavy processes into an integrated, risk-based and evidence-informed assessment lifecycle. It brings together technology risk, cybersecurity, security advisory, third-party risk, cloud and AI security, Governance, Risk and Compliance (GRC) modernization, adoption of ServiceNow Integrated Risk Management (IRM), data and automation, and leadership of a global team.

You Will Shape And Lead Six Connected Themes

Integrated Assessment Authority: One accountable leadership model for Threat Risk Assessment (TRA) and Vendor Security Review (VSR), with common direction, methods and risk language across specialized assessment teams.
Shift-left security assessment: Technology and cybersecurity risks identified and addressed earlier in architecture, design and delivery, when they are least costly to resolve.
Platform and application assessment: A two-level model that assesses shared platforms once and focuses application and vendor assessments on what is genuinely specific.
Evidence-informed risk decisions: Risk conclusions grounded in structured, verifiable evidence and consistent rating criteria rather than document volume.
Modern workflow, data and automation: Assessments run through modern ServiceNow IRM workflows, supported by structured data and the progressive use of AI and automation.
Portfolio risk insight: Clear, traceable reporting that surfaces recurring and systemic risks across the Bank's technology and third-party portfolio.

The Platform And Application Model Works At Two Levels

Horizontal assessments evaluate common platforms, shared services and approved technology patterns once, so related controls and evidence can be reused.
Vertical assessments evaluate the application, workload, project, vendor or material change, and focus on specific deviations, exposures and residual risks

Is this role right for you? In this role, you will:

Lead the existing TRA and VSR capabilities under one senior leadership model, preserving specialized expertise while establishing common direction, coordinated intake and triage, and shared standards.
Define and maintain consistent assessment methodology, risk-rating criteria, quality requirements, evidence principles and finding taxonomies, aligned to the Bank's technology control objectives and enterprise control library and to recognized frameworks such as the National Institute of Standards and Technology Cybersecurity Framework (NIST CSF), ISO/IEC 27001 and the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS).
Embed technology and cybersecurity assessment earlier in architecture, design and technology delivery, including the Bank's delivery framework, architecture review processes and Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery (CI/CD) pipelines.
Establish reusable security and platform patterns that allow downstream assessments to inherit approved baselines.
Assess material application-specific and vendor-specific risks, including data, identity, integration, architecture, exposure and residual risk.
Strengthen threat modelling and scenario-based risk analysis, using recognized approaches such as STRIDE and MITRE ATT&CK.
Act as the business owner for the technology-risk assessment capability within ServiceNow IRM, defining assessment requirements, workflows and data needs while working with the technical platform team, which owns platform configuration and delivery.
Lead the assessment-domain transition from legacy processes and repositories into modern IRM workflows, preserving application-to-assessment and application-to-risk traceability and establishing clear data-quality requirements.
Define risk-based triggers for reassessment following material change, significant vulnerability, control failure or deviation from an approved pattern.
Establish targeted post-implementation assurance for selected material controls, using authoritative evidence from accountable control owners and specialist functions.
Prioritize appropriate AI and automation opportunities across intake, triage, context extraction, pattern matching, assessment drafting, evidence orchestration and portfolio insight, in alignment with the Bank's enterprise artificial intelligence and technology-risk automation initiatives.
Identify recurring and systemic risks across the assessment portfolio and provide clear risk insight to technology leaders and governance forums.
Produce assessment outcomes that are timely, consistent, traceable, evidence-informed and defensible for regulatory, second-line, quality assurance and Internal Audit review, including under the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) Guideline B-13 and the New York State Department of Financial Services (NYDFS) Part 500 cybersecurity regulation, where applicable.
Lead and develop a large, multidisciplinary and geographically distributed team, building capabilities in security advisory, cloud and AI security, third-party security risk, methodology, data and automation..

Critical Partnerships

Success depends on strong partnerships across the Bank's three lines of defense. Each partner keeps its established mandate, and the Senior Director works with them to ensure that assessment conclusions are well-informed and aligned. Key partners include:

Technology leadership: Chief Information Officers (CIOs) and their delivery, architecture and engineering teams, the primary clients of the assessment capability.
Cybersecurity and architecture: The Office of the Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) and Enterprise Architecture, to align security standards, patterns and design guidance.
Control owners and control testing: Teams that implement and operate controls, and the Bank's technology control testing function, whose evidence informs assessment conclusions.
Technology risk management: Technology risk teams and Risk and Control Self-Assessment (RCSA) teams, which manage and aggregate technology risk across the Bank.
Platform and automation: The ServiceNow IRM platform and implementation teams, and the Bank's enterprise artificial intelligence and technology-risk automation initiatives, to ensure aligned workflows and data.
Governance and reporting: IT risk governance, issue management and reporting teams within the Office of the Chief Information Officer.
Independent oversight: Second-line risk management, Internal Quality Assurance (IQA) and Internal Audit, which provide independent challenge and assurance, and the teams that manage the Bank's regulatory relationships

Skills

Do you have the skills that will enable you to succeed in this role? We'd love to work with you if you have:

University degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Security or a related field.
10+ years of progressive experience in technology risk, cybersecurity or risk assessment, including senior leadership of technology or cybersecurity risk assessment functions.
Deep expertise in security advisory, assessment methodology and threat modelling at enterprise scale.
Strong experience in third-party and vendor security risk, and in cloud, AI, application and platform security.
A track record of leading enterprise GRC transformation, including with ServiceNow IRM or a comparable GRC platform, from business requirements through adoption.
Strong understanding of development, security and operations (DevSecOps) practices and secure-by-design principles.
Experience engaging regulators and Internal Audit in a highly regulated environment, ideally financial services.
Proven ability to lead large, distributed teams and to lead through influence across federated organizations and with senior technology executives.

Preferred Experience

Advanced degree or professional certifications such as Certified Information Systems Auditor (CISA), Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP), Certified in Risk and Information Systems Control (CRISC) or Certified Information Security Manager (CISM).
Experience leading platform- and pattern-based assessment models that allow controls to be inherited across applications and workloads.
Hands-on experience with risk data, evidence orchestration and workflow automation, including integrations with security tooling.
Familiarity with AI, machine learning and agentic AI applications in GRC, such as intake triage, artifact analysis, control mapping and risk-theme identification.
Experience applying structured risk-rating criteria, calibration and quantitative risk techniques.
Experience partnering with control-testing functions to integrate authoritative control evidence into risk assessment, ideally within a large financial institution

What's in it for you?

Diversity, Equity, Inclusion & Allyship - We strive to create an inclusive culture where every employee is empowered to reach their fullest potential, respected for who they are, and are embraced through bias-free practices and inclusive values across Scotiabank. We embrace diversity and provide opportunities for all employee to learn, grow & participate through our various Employee Resource Groups (ERGs) that span across diverse gender identities, ethnicity, race, age, ability & veterans.
Accessibility and Workplace Accommodations - We value the unique skills and experiences each individual brings to the Bank and are committed to creating and maintaining an inclusive and accessible environment for everyone. Scotiabank continues to locate, remove and prevent barriers so that we can build a diverse and inclusive environment while meeting accessibility requirements.
Upskilling through online courses, cross-functional development opportunities, and tuition assistance.
Competitive Rewards program including bonus, flexible vacation, personal, sick days and benefits will start on day one.
Community Engagement - no matter where you choose to work from; we offer opportunities for community engagement & belonging with our various programs such as hackathons, contests, Humans of Digital and much more.

Location(s): Canada : Ontario : Toronto

Guided by our purpose: "for every future", we help our customers, their families and their communities achieve success through a broad range of advice, products and services, including personal and commercial banking, wealth management and private banking, corporate and investment banking, and capital markets.

The Director, Global Hosting Services, defines, leads, and governs Deloitte Global’s private-cloud hosting strategy, data center and cloud networking services, and Global Wide Area Network (GWAN). The role oversees secure, resilient connectivity among Deloitte Global hosting facilities, member-firm environments, and cloud service provider (CSP) hubs across Azure, AWS, and Google Cloud. The Director also leads CSP cost reporting and invoice reconciliation through the Deloitte Cloud Services (DCS) Cloud Business Office, supports agile delivery of platform and network enhancements, and ensures operational excellence and rapid incident response across these services.

Key Responsibilities:

Deloitte Cloud Services (DCS) Networking

Oversee the design and implementation of network architecture supporting DCS hubs, connectivity among Deloitte environments, the internet, and cloud service providers, and secure access to cloud-hosted services, including firewalls and load balancers:
Multi-CSP connectivity
Inter-CSP connectivity
Secure hybrid-cloud IPv4/IPv6 connectivity
CSP inter-region global connectivity
CSP intra-region scalability
IP addressing management

Lead the team in delivering these services, with operational excellence and 24/7 monitoring and support.
Drive continuous improvement and automation through API enhancements and agentic AI solutions to reduce service-delivery time and enable proactive monitoring, rapid issue identification, and resolution.

What will your typical day look like?

Interfirm Network Service (GWAN)

Lead the Interfirm Network Service (INS), providing seamless, secure, resilient, and optimized connectivity among member firms and across public-cloud environments.
Develop solution roadmaps and architectures that address evolving business needs, technology requirements, cybersecurity threats, and demand for high-performance, low-latency connectivity.
Drive operational service excellence, support member-firm disaster recovery testing exercises, and adapt connectivity options as firms implement local in-country WAN and SD-WAN solutions.
Manage IPv4/IPv6 address allocation for member firms and countries.

Deloitte Cloud Services (DCS) Cloud Business Office

Provide scaled agile delivery services supporting product enhancements for DCS platform, product, and networking teams, as well as Global Enterprise Cloud Management Services.
Lead Cloud Business Office delivery of CSP cost insights for member firms, CSP invoice reconciliation, and billing to Deloitte entities. Support FinOps through cost-optimization recommendations, CSP cost reporting, and AI token-ledger reporting.

Risk Management & Compliance

Ensure all data center and cloud-platform solutions comply with global regulatory, security, and privacy standards.
Proactively identify risks and implement mitigation strategies.
Serve as a trusted liaison to Cyber teams on cloud-related matters, champion Cyber initiatives, and review and provide feedback on Cyber standards and programs.

Private Cloud Delivery (Colocation Services)

Define and continuously evolve Deloitte Global’s private-hosting and colocation strategy, including regional services in the United States and Germany. Adapt the strategy to emerging requirements such as zero-trust networking, private infrastructure supporting GPU-intensive AI workloads, and future quantum-computing capabilities.
Lead the team in delivering these services while maintaining operational excellence and compliance with audit, SOC, and ISO requirements.
Develop private-cloud roadmaps, standards, and reference architectures, and establish governance frameworks, policies, and cost-recovery processes.
